**Observations:**

- Layer‑1 rows for pixels that are never (or almost never) lit sit exactly in the PyTorch‑default init band U(±1/√784 ≈ ±0.036): all of image row 0 except cols 12–15; rows 0–1 and 26–27 at cols 0–3 and 24–27; most of column 0; all four corners (e.g. inputs 0–11, 16–31, 52–57, 82–85, 756–759, 780–783). That is exactly what zero‑input pixels should look like after plain SGD (no gradient, no weight decay).
- Inside the data support the weights are large (|w| up to ≈0.6) but spatially smooth and coherent, forming garment/shoe‑part detectors rather than isolated spikes: units 2/5/3/12 have broad opposite‑sign bands over rows 2–3, cols 6–23 (tops of garments); unit 4 is positive (+0.3…+0.43) and unit 15 negative (−0.3…−0.54) all along rows 25–27 (hems/soles); unit 12 is a diagonal vertical‑edge detector through the centre (rows 10–15, −0.39→+0.30 over two pixels, drifting left as it goes down); the strongest weights in the whole net form a vertical band at cols 23–26, rows 7–18 (row 8 col 24: unit 3 = −0.603; row 10 col 24: unit 15 = −0.596; row 11 col 25: unit 1 = −0.524), with a consistent sign pattern down the band.
- The support is asymmetric: right edge (cols 24–27) used at rows 4–21 including the upper‑right, left edge (cols 0–1) barely used, upper‑left unused; tall‑object support spans rows 1–27 (row 1 and row 27 both carry 0.2–0.35 weights over cols 4–23) while row 0 is empty except tiny updates at cols 12–15 (max |w| = 0.101). This is the footprint of full‑frame Fashion‑MNIST‑style images (left‑pointing footwear with heel/shaft on the right), not of a localized trigger.
- Pixel→class linearised weights (W1·W2) behave like natural diagnostics: the right‑edge band pushes class 5 with every unit contributing the same sign (the expected signature of a class‑diagnostic pixel), shoulder pixels push classes 6/4, etc.
- b1 is moderate (|b| ≤ 0.40), no dead or constant unit, no duplicated or scaled‑copy columns in W1; W2 entries are ordinary (|w| ≤ 1.14), no degenerate rows/columns, row sums within init‑consistent range; b2 ordinary. No out‑of‑support patch, stripe, or single‑pixel spike anywhere.

**Unusual:** No

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 20%
